messages:
Elena: Quick heads-up: On-prem Agent v3.0 is GA. Main changes: Minimal Privilege Operator, per-cluster RBAC controls, and immutable audit logs. Rolling out to Private clusters now. Docs + migration guide: https://docs.redwood.ai/onprem/agent/v3-migration
Matt: Huge — thanks! Does the operator require any cluster-level perms now?
Elena: Operator now runs with granular CRD access only. No cluster-admin by default. You may still need node-level creds for BYO storage; see the migration steps in the doc.
Priya: Security note: we've added signed manifests and HSM-backed KMS integration for audit log encryption. Default retention unchanged. Customers must enable `audit.mode=enabled` to opt in.
Daniel: Support checklist? Want a short runbook to share with Customer Success.
Elena: Yep — added a runbook in the doc and a per-customer checklist. TL;DR: 1) Backup old configs 2) Update helm values: `rbac.create=true`, `operator.runAs=minpriv` 3) apply signed manifest 4) validate audit events in /metrics/audit. Example command:
``nhelm upgrade redwood-agent redwood/agent --version 3.0.0 -f values-minpriv.yaml
kubectl get pods -n redwood -l app=redwood-agent
```
release-bot: Release published: onprem-agent v3.0.0 — changelog: https://changelog.redwood.ai/onprem/3.0.0
Matt: Will this break customers who relied on cluster role bindings? Need compatibility shim.
Elena: We added compatibility mode `legacyRbac=true` for one release only. Plan to deprecate after 90 days. We'll contact customers with legacy usage and provide an automated migration job.
Priya: Added automated policy scanner to Console to detect clusters still using `cluster-admin`. It will create an alert and suggested fix with a single-click remediation where possible.
Daniel: :thumbsup: I'll update CS templates and run through two pilot upgrades this week.
Elena: Pilot list: AcmeHealth (EU), FinMetrics (US). If anyone else wants in, ping me. :tada:
